speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Dixmier operators and Grinevich’s construction
summary: The opening of the manuscript dated 23 February 1981 reports Dixmier’s commuting operators of orders four and six, then Grinevich’s extension using Tyurin parameters. The catalogue places this record in 1991; the autograph date and the surrounding 1981 sequence establish a catalogue decade error. This recovered entry precedes Cherednik’s talk in manuscript order.

speaker: I. V. Cherednik
title: Inverse scattering, elliptic zero curvature, and Yang–Baxter structures
summary: Cherednik presents three stages of soliton theory, from scalar inverse scattering through matrix zero curvature to the Yang--Baxter equation, with elliptic examples and Landau--Lifshitz dynamics. Only the upper portion of P000961 belongs here; Khovanskii begins below it. The manuscript dates this material 23 February 1981, correcting the catalogue’s 1991 date.

speaker: I. V. Cherednik
title: A diagram relating Yang–Baxter structures
summary: A short diagrammatic reprise links factorized scattering, two-dimensional statistical mechanics, quantum one-dimensional systems, and integrable equations. Belavin adds unitarity. Gelfand’s preceding Gaussian-tail exercise is retained here as an explicitly attributed intervention; his adjacent Kazarnovskii question is indexed with record 513. The detailed three-stage account is in recovered record 510, not this March entry.

speaker: A. A. Belavin
title: Inversion, crossing, and Baxter invariant curves
summary: Belavin studies matrix inversion and partial transposition, then the invariant quantities of the symmetric eight-vertex matrix. Elliptic curves appear after projectivizing and imposing generic smoothness. The notebook’s symmetry sign and the distinction between generic and exceptional orbits require qualification.

speaker: I. V. Cherednik
title: Factorized scattering and commuting transfer operators
summary: The continuation derives the Yang--Baxter relation from three-particle reordering, rewrites it in tensor notation, gives an elliptic Pauli-matrix solution, and states the commuting-transfer-operator mechanism. The index in the component relation and the tensor leg traced in the last theorem are faithfully recorded mathematical errors, not transcription mistakes.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Moser’s isospectral formulation of ellipsoid geodesics
summary: Gelfand discusses Moser’s contribution to the Chern Symposium, giving the constrained geodesic equation and a projected matrix with constant spectrum. Jacobi’s earlier integration is mentioned; the displayed matrix construction is the modern Moser formulation.

speaker: P. G. Grinevich
title: Rational commuting differential operators of rank two
summary: Grinevich explains the elliptic rank-two Krichever--Novikov construction in Tyurin parameters and its rational specializations. The Dixmier case is a choice of rational parameter, not a consequence of setting the centre parameter to zero alone.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: A Dixmier formula and algebraic curves in the Weyl division ring
summary: Kirillov gives a formal pseudodifferential description, followed by the question of rational commuting operators with a prescribed genus-two spectral curve. Gelfand proposes an embedding of the function field of any algebraic curve in the rank-one Weyl division ring. The sixth-order formula needs emendation, and the universal curve assertion remains distinct from results for generic genus-two curves or some curves of every genus.

speaker: J.-L. Brylinski
title: Verma modules and geometric realization
summary: The uncertain handwritten surname is resolved by the explicit Kashiwara collaboration and the subject. The short record defines Verma modules and gestures toward realizations on the flag variety, with an SL(2) example. It does not state a new proof of the Kazhdan--Lusztig formula.

speaker: E. Viehweg
title: Classification of threefolds after Esnault’s Bourbaki report
summary: The talk explicitly follows Hélène Esnault’s February 1981 Bourbaki exposition. Kodaira dimension, irregularity, abelian varieties, and Albanese fibrations of threefolds are summarized. A question mark in the irregularity-zero case is preserved as an incomplete classification entry, not promoted to a newly formulated conjecture.

speaker: C. Kassel
title: K-theory of spaces and arithmetic K-groups
summary: The manuscript has separate headings for Christian Kassel and Christophe Soulé, although the catalogue supplies only the Kassel record. Kassel reports Waldhausen’s programme and homotopy-ring constructions. Soulé’s contribution concerns orders of K-groups of the integers and zeta values; its bibliographic shorthand is not an exact identification of an Inventiones paper dated February 1980.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: The collisionless Vlasov description
summary: A brief introduction explains a self-consistent field generated by many charged particles whose binary collisions are neglected. The record states a modelling principle, not a quantified mean-field limit theorem.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Weinstein’s Hamiltonian formulations of continua
summary: Arnold begins with the geodesic interpretation of incompressible Euler flow, then describes reduction to coadjoint orbits and the extension to Vlasov and gauge-coupled kinetic equations. The density variable required for compressible fluid mechanics is mentioned but no full bracket is written.

speaker: A. V. Bobylev
title: Maxwell molecules and Fourier methods for Boltzmann’s equation
summary: Bobylev presents the spatially homogeneous collision equation and singles out inverse-fourth-power potentials. Fourier methods, Gaussian convolution, linearization, and the isotropic nonlinear hierarchy appear, together with remarks on exact solutions and hydrodynamic limits. Angular cutoff, function-space, and normalization assumptions must be supplied when interpreting the compact-operator claim.

speaker: B. V. Lidskii
title: Spectra of sums of Hermitian matrices
summary: Lidskii announces the recursive Horn inequalities and a connection with tensor-product multiplicities. His two-page announcement appeared in 1982, but the later literature distinguishes it from a published proof. Klyachko’s work and the Knutson--Tao saturation theorem provide the established resolution.

speaker: S. G. Krein
title: Compressible fluids, shocks, and dispersive step evolution
summary: Krein reports the diffeomorphism-group approach to compressible flow and the incompressible limit. Scalar characteristics and shock formation prompt interventions by Gelfand and Zakharov. Gelfand’s final question concerns step-like data for a polynomial regularization of Burgers’ equation; the polynomial is not specified, so distinct dispersive and dissipative cases must be separated.

speaker: G. I. Olshanskii
title: Invariant cones, Lie semigroups, and highest-weight representations
summary: Olshanskii develops semigroups of contractions, invariant cones in Hermitian Lie algebras, and holomorphic extension of unitary highest-weight representations. The primary paper was received in December 1980 and published in 1981. Properness of cones, a choice of sign, and the analytic representation category are essential qualifications absent from the shorthand notes.
